content.text:
Round 2 planning. We need to test the director's proposed next step: apply the H1 cheap pre-filter to the full 1,362-candidate pool, then run compare_strategies (random vs surrogate) on the filtered sub-pool.

## Context from Round 1 (cite record IDs below)
- Pool: 1,362 candidates, 129 hits, base rate 9.47%, 8,660 prior calcs. Source: JARVIS-DFT dft_3d doi:10.1016/j.commatsci.2025.114063 (record f0f51395)
- H1 filter [record 050e0686]: OptB88vdW gap ∈ [0.7, 1.2] eV AND direct_gap = True AND ns² cation ∈ {Bi, Sb, Sn, Ge, Cu}
- Round 1 retrospective result [record 05099ec9]: random 106.8 calcs, heuristic 47.6 (2.11×), surrogate-on-full-pool 33.8 (2.99×). H1 filter params were silently dropped — H3 (pre-filter + surrogate) was never tested.
- Skeptic verdict [record 7ba476fb]: TRUSTED WITH CAVEATS; primary recommendation: rerun on H1-filtered sub-pool to test H3.
- Director next step [record c70fa954]: pre-filter pool → compare_strategies(strategies=[random,surrogate], seeds=10, leakage_guard=true) on filtered sub-pool.

## Your task
Design TWO candidate test options for Round 2, pick one, and specify the exact runner call:

Option A: Use apply_filter(gap_min=0.7, gap_max=1.2, direct_gap=True, ns2_cations=[Bi,Sb,Sn,Ge,Cu]) to produce a filtered sub-pool, then compare_strategies(strategies=[random,surrogate], seeds=10, leakage_guard=True, target_hits=10) on that sub-pool.

Option B: Same filter but also test a 'heuristic' strategy arm on the sub-pool (random vs heuristic vs surrogate on filtered pool) to see whether BO adds value beyond filter-only.

For each option specify: (a) oracle budget cost (zero for retrospective), (b) what we learn, (c) failure modes. Pick one by expected learning per cost. We MUST measure H1 filter recall (hits retained / 129 total hits) alongside speedup — this is required reporting per lab rules.

Output: chosen option, exact tool call parameters, success criterion, failure action.

|---|---|---|
| **What it tests** | Recalibrated gap-only [0.5, 1.5] eV filter + BO surrogate vs random | Same + heuristic arm; tests whether filter makes heuristic redundant |

| **Failure mode** | Leaves heuristic-filter interaction untested before live spend | ~15 s longer; heuristic arm may prove redundant — but that's the finding, not a cost |

**H1 filter recall:** N/A — H1 was aborted. New filter recall = 61.2% (79/129, record `286d17bb`), above the 60% gate.

## Choice: Option B

Option B strictly dominates Option A at identical cost (zero oracle budget, one retrospective benchmark call). On the enriched 275-candidate pool (28.7% base rate vs 9.47% full-pool), the heuristic's sorting advantage may already be captured by the filter — or the two may stack. The 3-way result directly informs whether Round 4 deploys filter+surrogate, filter+heuristic, or pivots to H2, eliminating an otherwise mandatory extra benchmark round.
